## What the chronicles say [Record]

Kęstutis was found dead at Krėva on 15 August 1382, the feast of the Assumption, about twelve days after the arrest of 3 August (some sources say "a week later"). [Jogaila](../characters/jogaila.qmd) claimed that his uncle had hanged himself, which few believed. VLE says he was killed (strangled); the Lithuanian Wikipedia has him strangled on the orders of Julijona or Skirgaila, the body burned in Vilnius; the Order's chronicler Wigand of Marburg is the main near-contemporary. Whether he died "naturally or was murdered" is stated as debated in the English Wikipedia; most historians accept murder. The body was cremated with pagan rites in Vilnius, according to tradition. Skirgaila found the body.

## What really happened [Saga]

[Henė](../characters/hanulas.qmd)'s Breath of the Void muffled the tower so that no struggle was heard, and a shard of Velnias strangled the duke while the guards slept in unnatural stupor (mythic_gaps §1). Four Rus' mercenaries, paid in Riga silver, strangle him with the golden chain whose clasp bears the Riga mark of two crossed keys under a cross. Kęstutis, who took the beggar's coin knowing, says: Gabija will not shine on your masters today; the cowards are Skirgaila and Jogaila. [Birutė](../characters/birute.qmd) appears as an apparition leading his soul. The wolves of the Dykra howl. It is the kin-murder that breaks clause 2 of the Silent Pact: no Gediminid sheds Gediminid blood. The gods' protection lapses and the Shadow-Seller collects.

## Consequences

Caused by [the arrest](ev_arrest.qmd). It breaks [clause 2 of the Silent Pact](../magic/silent_pact.qmd) and leads to [Perkūnas claiming Vytautas](ev_perkunas_mark.qmd) and to [the escape from Krėva](ev_kreva_escape.qmd). It also sets Skirgaila and Jogaila on the road that ends in the 1385 Union signed above the cell, and Žygimantas in the cell in 1438.

## Dramatisation

Book I ch. 8 "Krėvos Požemiai" (Kęstutis and Vytautas, talking through the stones; about ten to fourteen August), ch. 9 "Paskutinė Giesmė" (Kęstutis, then Vytautas; the night of 14–15 August; Žolinė eve), ch. 10 "Šaltas Rytas" (Vytautas; the morning of 15 August). Echoes: ch. 28b (Vytautas in the cell, 1385), Book I ch. 30 (Skirgaila), Book V ch. 19 (Žygimantas).
